evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese reconstruction dataset
evidence.text: In the Baxter–Sagart 2014 dataset, 八 has Mandarin pinyin bā, Middle Chinese transcription peat, and Old Chinese reconstruction *pˤret. The authors explain that the Middle Chinese column transcribes information from medieval sources and is not itself a reconstruction. The supplied local table has the same 八 row: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, character 八.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese reconstruction dataset
evidence.text: In the Baxter–Sagart 2014 dataset, 半 has Mandarin pinyin bàn, Middle Chinese transcription panH, and Old Chinese reconstruction *pˤan-s. The Old Chinese form shares *pˤ- with 八 *pˤret but has a different ending; these readings alone do not establish 八’s phonetic role in 半. The supplied local table has the same 半 row: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, character 半.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（香港中文大學人文電算研究中心）
evidence.text: The entry describes Spring and Autumn bronze forms as 八 plus 牛, reads 八 as both division-related semantic element and sound element, and attributes to 何琳儀 the proposal that 半 is an early graph of 判. It proposes ‘split/open’ as the original sense extended to ‘half.’ It also reports variants substituting 斗 or 升 for 牛 and another form substituting shape-similar 刃 for 斗. These are the database’s analyses; it does not establish a complete dated sequence or date the semantic transition.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：半

search_audit.outcome: Search surfaced the primary Baxter–Sagart dataset and a scholarly phonetic-elements paper. Opened the Baxter–Sagart PDF and checked its key and 八 entry; opened the CUHK 半 record and checked its component, variant, and semantic-analysis text. The official Unicode per-character lookup URLs for 八 and 半 both returned internal errors and could not verify the exact kMandarin rows. Those modern readings are therefore reported only from supplied local Unihan rows.

gaps: Official Unicode per-character Unihan records for 八 and 半 were inaccessible; the exact current readings are supported by supplied local rows, not an inspected external click-through page.
The checked Baxter–Sagart reconstructions share an initial but differ in their endings; this comparison does not independently prove the proposed phonetic role of 八.
The CUHK account proposes a ‘split/open’ to ‘half’ semantic development, but the inspected source supplies no dated sequence establishing when it occurred.
